feedback: If the prediction was 'the stronger one always looks brighter': 'The near torch looked as bright as, or brighter than, the stronger lamp. How bright a light LOOKS depends on distance as well as power.'
If the prediction was 'the near one might win because it's closer': 'Exactly — being close can make a weaker light look brighter than a stronger, far one.'
Connect back: 'This is why the Sun looks brightest of all stars: it is the nearest, not the most powerful.'
activities.intendedInsight: Everyday lights obey the same rule as stars: how bright something looks depends on both its power and its distance. A prediction of 'the stronger one always looks brighter' shows power and distance have not yet been separated.
learnerActions: Before anything is switched on, look at a small dim torch set close to where you sit and a much brighter lamp placed far across the room.
PREDICT which light will LOOK brighter from your seat, and say WHY.
Switch both on and observe: the weaker near torch can look as bright as or brighter than the powerful distant lamp.
Compare what actually happened with your prediction and revise your reasoning if needed.
Answer: which light is really more powerful, and which one LOOKS brighter from here?
activities.title: Torch vs floodlight: predict, observe, explain
